answer_text:
Here's a comprehensive guide to the **best sources for free 3D game assets** in 2026! 🎮

---

## 🏆 Top Free 3D Game Asset Websites

### 1. 🟡 [Kenney.nl](https://kenney.nl)
This one-person operation has released over **40,000 assets** — all CC0, all free, no sign-up required. The art style is clean, colorful, and remarkably consistent across packs, which means you can mix and match assets without your game looking inconsistent. The site offers 2D assets, 3D models, UI elements, fonts, and audio. There are also free tools like **Asset Forge** for creating your own 3D models.
> ✅ Best for: Rapid prototyping, consistent art style, UI elements

---

### 2. 🔵 [Quaternius](https://quaternius.com)
Quaternius provides a large collection of **low-poly 3D models** that are completely free to use under the CC0 license. You can use them for any project, personal or commercial, without needing to give credit. The consistent, clean art style makes these assets perfect for prototyping or games with a stylized look. Assets come rigged and animated, ready to drop into **Unity, Unreal, or Godot**.
> ✅ Best for: Low-poly 3D games, animated characters, stylized aesthetics

---

### 3. 🟢 [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com)
Poly Haven started as HDRI Haven and has grown into a comprehensive library of **3D models, HDRIs, and textures** — all CC0. The models tend toward realistic props and environmental pieces rather than stylized game assets, but they're high quality and instantly usable. No sign-up required. Just download what you need.
> ✅ Best for: Realistic 3D assets, environment art, lighting references

---

### 4. 🟠 [Sketchfab](https://sketchfab.com)
Sketchfab is a huge repository of 3D models with a large collection of downloadable assets. While many are for sale, there's a substantial number of models available for free. The platform's built-in **3D viewer** is a great feature, allowing you to inspect every angle of a model before you download it. Just be sure to check the licensing for each model, as they can vary.
> ✅ Best for: Browsing a massive variety of 3D community models

---

### 5. 🟣 [itch.io](https://itch.io/game-assets/free/tag-3d)
Itch.io is a popular platform for indie game developers to host and sell their games, but it also has a massive section for game assets. You can find a wide variety of free 3D game assets, from character models to environmental packs, often with very permissive licenses. The community-driven nature of Itch.io means you'll discover unique and creative assets you won't find anywhere else.
> ✅ Best for: Unique, creative, community-made packs

---

### 6. 🔴 [Mixamo](https://www.mixamo.com) (by Adobe)
Mixamo offers **2,000+ free animations** with auto-rigging, making it ideal for bringing characters to life quickly.
> ✅ Best for: Character animations, auto-rigging

---

### 7. 🟤 [OpenGameArt](https://opengameart.org)
OpenGameArt has been around for over a decade and hosts a massive collection of **2D art, 3D models, music, and sound effects** — all under open licences like CC0, CC-BY, or GPL.
> ✅ Best for: Open-source projects, large variety, hidden gems

---

### 8. ⚫ [Quixel Megascans](https://quixel.com)
Quixel is releasing a final, offline version of Quixel Mixer, along with the option to **download over 800 free Quixel Megascans assets**. It's a pioneer in photogrammetry-based 3D assets, delivering photorealistic models compatible with any engine, as well as leading tools like Blender, Maya, and Houdini. All assets are scanned from real-world objects using purpose-built hardware.
> ✅ Best for: AAA-quality photorealistic assets

---

### 9. ⬜ [Unity Asset Store (Free Section)](https://assetstore.unity.com)
The Unity Asset Store's free section offers **10,000+ Unity-optimized assets**, covering characters, environments, props, and more.
> ✅ Best for: Unity developers looking for ready-to-use, engine-optimized assets

---

### 10. 🟦 [Free3D](https://free3d.com)
A large number of their models have a lower polygon count and can be used in games straight away. Categories include Architecture, Vehicles, Weapons, Animals, Plants, and more.
> ✅ Best for: A wide variety of categorized 3D models

---

## 📋 Quick License Guide
Here's what the licenses mean:
- **CC0 (Public Domain)** – Use commercially, modify freely, no attribution required
- **CC BY (Attribution)** – Use commercially, modify freely, but must credit the creator
- **CC BY-SA** – Use commercially, modify freely, but must credit AND share modifications under the same license

---

## 💡 Pro Tips
- Choose assets from the **same creator or pack** (e.g., all Quaternius or all Kenney) and don't mix photorealistic and low-poly cartoon styles.
- **GLB/glTF** are the recommended formats — all textures, materials, and animations are bundled in one file, with native support in Three.js, Babylon.js, Unity, and Unreal Engine.
- Always **verify license compatibility** before commercial use and maintain an asset documentation spreadsheet (source, license, attribution).

Happy game developing! 🚀
